experiment.subtitle: One computed decode step at batch sizes 1, 10, 100, 200, and 500.

sources.label: NVIDIA H200 Tensor Core GPU specifications

contract: All sequences in each measured batch enter one native batched /generate call.
max_new_tokens=2 represents one fake handoff token and one computed decode step.
Useful work excludes every CUDA graph launched after the matched Finish boundary.
limitations: Kernel residency is captured device time, not CUDA occupancy or wall latency.
B=200 and B=500 use 832-token contexts; comparisons against the 4,096-token B=1/10/100 capture combine batch-size and context-length changes.
Tree MFU and MBUmin are static lower-bound models, not Nsight Compute counter measurements.
Routed expert IDs were not retained, so multi-request expert-weight bytes use a maximum-reuse lower bound.
Kernel-active token rate is a GPU-0 trace normalization, not serving throughput or TPOT.
Interval unions are computed independently per tree node and are not additive across overlapping siblings.
Batches captured at different context lengths are not a controlled batch-only scaling experiment.

observations: GPU 0 interval union is the primary timing boundary throughout this report.
Graph wall span, idle gaps, and overlap-additive residency remain diagnostics only.
Client HTTP timing is excluded from every displayed latency, rate, and scaling ratio.
Every tab carries its own context-token count; comparisons across different contexts combine batch and context effects.
comparison.headline: Headline time is GPU 0 active-kernel interval union: concurrent kernels are merged once, while HTTP latency and GPU-idle gaps are excluded. Context differs by tab, so comparisons against B=1 are not pure batch-only measurements.
comparison.interpretation: For each batch, kernel-active rate is B divided by the same GPU-0 active-union time. Therefore time increase multiplied by rate increase equals batch-size increase, apart from display rounding. This identity does not remove context-length differences between captures.

experiment.title: GLM-5.2 FP8 TP=8 B=20 EAGLE Decode
experiment.subtitle: One selected steady speculative-decode cycle with real 4K KV-cache prefixes.
experiment.precision: FP8 target with BF16 MLA work normalized to FP8-equivalent

sources.label: NVIDIA H200 Tensor Core GPU specifications

contract: Twenty requests use genuine 4,096-token prefixes: 4,032 cached tokens plus a 64-token recomputed tail per sequence.
EAGLE uses five speculative steps, top-k one, and six draft candidates per request.
The selected steady cycle is draft proposal → target verification → acceptance/KV commit → draft-state catch-up.
Target verification runs one full 78-layer model pass over 20 × 6 = 120 candidate rows.
limitations: The selected cycle is a GPU-0 module-efficiency scope, not end-to-end serving TPOT.
Average acceptance length is measured over the full request, not reconstructed for this individual cycle.
MFU and MBU minimum use static modeled numerators and theoretical H200 peak denominators.

checks.name: Measured request and real batch
checks.evidence: HTTP 200; 20 responses; exact prompt, completion, and request-ID accounting.

checks.name: Real KV-cache prefixes
checks.evidence: Every sequence reused exactly 4,032 cached tokens and recomputed a 64-token tail.

checks.name: Selected-cycle ownership
checks.evidence: 4,231 GPU-0 events assigned exactly once across four non-overlapping phases and 320 tree nodes.

checks.name: Target verification across ranks
checks.evidence: All eight TP ranks contain 3,709 classified target events and the same 78-layer refresh/reuse ledger.

checks.name: Privacy boundary
checks.evidence: No raw prompt text, token IDs, response text, or private prefix corpus is published.

comparison.headline: B=20 EAGLE is a separate speculative-decode execution mode: its primary time is one selected GPU-0 four-phase cycle, not one standard-decode step.
observations: Target verification dominates the selected cycle and evaluates 120 candidate rows in one 78-layer pass.
The sequence-cycle rate divides 20 requested sequences by cycle active union; it does not multiply by average acceptance length.
Use the execution tree for phase and kernel efficiency; do not place this tab on the native B=1 scaling identity.

kernel_timing.non_comparable_reason: EAGLE executes a draft/verify/accept/catch-up cycle, while the native tabs contain one standard-decode model step.

notes: The complete four-phase cycle is embedded for GPU 0. All eight ranks were independently audited for the 3,709-launch target-verification graph.
MFU normalizes mixed work to dense H200 FP8; BF16 MLA work counts twice.
MBU minimum uses a modeled useful-byte floor, not measured DRAM traffic.
The selected-cycle efficiency scope is one GPU rank; target verification alone was cross-rank audited.
Real-prefix admission is excluded from the selected steady-cycle timing.
The trace contains 54 complete EAGLE cycles; zero-based cycle 2 is expanded.
Every selected-cycle GPU-0 event is assigned to exactly one of four phases and one tree leaf.

phase_roles.attention: DP-attention lanes partition the global request batch
phase_roles.moe: TP8/EP8 model-parallel routed and shared expert execution
phase_roles.output: DP hidden-state zero-fill/copy + AllReduce before LM head; TP vocabulary AllGather after LM head

contract: DP attention is enabled; global B=100 is distributed across eight local DP lanes.
Audit-derived local real batches: B=12 × 4 lanes, B=13 × 4 lanes; every physical CUDA graph runs B=13.
Each sequence returns one fake handoff token and one GPU-computed decode token.
No prefill work or speculative decoding belongs to the selected generation.
limitations: No module NVTX ranges label individual graph nodes; ownership is a validated reconstruction from kernel motifs and stream evidence.
Raw residency includes overlap and possible dependency-sensitive time; it is not critical-path or isolated arithmetic latency.
Batch padding is contract-derived. Standard server rows may expose the physical padded batch but do not prove which rank received each real local batch size.
MFU/MBU are intentionally absent: this scaffold has no approved model FLOP or byte numerator for the new B=100 trace.
The detailed GPU0 tree is one representative physical B=13 replay; it is not the full B=100 timing boundary.
The complete DP8 capture is independent and not directly comparable with the native DP1 B=1 timing identity.
Graphless kernels are outside the audited full-model boundary and are not classified as cleanup.

comparison.headline: This tab is the independently measured TP8/DP8/EP8 B=100 capture. Every panel uses its 4,096-token, complete full-model evidence.
observations: The primary computed-token rate uses 100 useful tokens over the complete full-model envelope; HTTP time is excluded.
The GPU0 execution tree is one representative physical B=13 replay and has its own local timing diagnostics.
Cross-B1 time/rate identity is unavailable because topology, local work, and context differ.
MFU and MBU remain unavailable until reviewed FLOP/byte numerators or hardware counters exist.

provenance.boundary_note: The tree contains one complete representative GPU-0 graph-family-2 execution (correlation 41862). Global B=100 is distributed over DP8; this physical graph computes 13 local rows at 4,096 context tokens. It is not an eight-rank summed timeline.

kernel_timing.non_comparable_reason: DP8 uses a complete eight-device envelope while native DP1 uses one GPU's active union. The timing boundary and topology differ.

notes: The complete view contains all 3 audited scheduler wave(s) and all 24 full-model graph replays; the detailed tree is one representative GPU-0 replay.
Per-rank interval unions are measured independently; their sum is not the global critical path.
No MFU, MBU, modeled FLOPs, modeled bytes, or HBM counters are claimed.
The complete view contains all 3 audited scheduler wave(s) and all 24 full-model graph replays; the detailed tree is one representative GPU-0 replay.
